input: Get a referral for a sleep specialist this month

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Knowing the specific sleep issue (insomnia, sleep apnea, restless legs, etc.) determines what type of specialist or referral pathway is needed.
Whether the user has a current primary care physician or GP determines whether they can request a referral directly or need to establish care first.
Insurance type and coverage rules (e.g., HMO requiring referrals vs. PPO allowing self-referral) completely change the steps involved.
A specific deadline within the month (e.g., before the 15th vs. end of month) affects how urgently the first action needs to happen.
Whether the user prefers an in-person appointment or telehealth affects which doctors and platforms are viable options.
Knowing if 'done' means referral in hand, appointment booked, or first consultation completed clarifies the finish line.
Whether the user has already spoken to their doctor about this issue determines whether they are starting from scratch or following up on an existing conversation.

gold.taskTitle: Get a sleep specialist referral this month
gold.taskDescription: The user wants to obtain a referral to see a sleep specialist within the current month.

questions.title: What specific sleep problem are you seeking help for?
questions.description: Identify the sleep issue (e.g., insomnia, suspected sleep apnea, excessive daytime sleepiness) to determine the right type of specialist and referral pathway.

questions.title: Do you have a primary care doctor you can contact?
questions.description: Determine whether the user has an existing GP or PCP relationship, or whether they need to establish care first before requesting a referral.

questions.title: What type of health insurance do you have?
questions.description: Understand whether the plan (HMO, PPO, etc.) requires a formal referral from a PCP or allows direct specialist booking, as this drives the entire process.

questions.title: Is there a specific date by which you need this done?
questions.description: Clarify urgency within the month so the plan can prioritize immediate actions appropriately.

questions.title: Do you prefer an in-person visit or a telehealth appointment?
questions.description: Determine the preferred format for both the referral conversation and the specialist visit, which affects which providers are viable.

questions.title: What does success look like — referral received, or appointment booked?
questions.description: Clarify the finish line so the plan knows whether to stop at obtaining the referral document or continue through to scheduling with the specialist.

questions.title: Have you already brought up this issue with your doctor?
questions.description: Find out if this is a fresh conversation or a follow-up, which determines whether the first step is a new appointment or a simple callback/message.
